# Overview

```{=html}
<div id="trm-structure-summary" class="trm-structure-cards"></div>
<div class="trm-structure-note">
Components are coordinate-supported hypotheses. “Composite candidate” and
“nested candidate” are not confirmed biological structures until reads or an
assembled insertion sequence demonstrate linkage between components.
</div>
```

# Structure landscape

Every insertion sequence is available below as a paginated structure map (50 per page). The default
ordering brings multi-component and alternative-rich signals to the top, but
does not hide unresolved sequences or sequences without a TE match. Filters
only narrow this landscape when a specific question needs to be tested.

```{=html}
<p id="trm-structure-status" role="status" aria-live="polite">Loading report data…</p>
<fieldset id="trm-structure-filters" class="trm-structure-toolbar" disabled>
  <legend class="visually-hidden">Filter insertion structures</legend>
  <label>Chromosome <select id="trm-structure-chrom"><option value="">All</option></select></label>
  <label>TE family <select id="trm-structure-te"><option value="">All</option></select></label>
  <label>Classification <select id="trm-structure-class"><option value="">All</option></select></label>
  <label>Final call <select id="trm-structure-final"><option value="">All</option><option value="yes">Reported only</option><option value="no">Unreported only</option></select></label>
  <label>Minimum components <input id="trm-structure-min-components" type="number" min="0" value="0"></label>
  <label>Search <input id="trm-structure-search" type="search" placeholder="event, TE, location…"></label>
  <label>Order <select id="trm-structure-sort"><option value="signal">Most informative first</option><option value="position">Genomic position</option><option value="components">Most components</option><option value="length">Longest insertion</option></select></label>
</fieldset>
<div class="trm-structure-toolbar-footer">
  <strong id="trm-structure-filter-note"></strong>
  <button id="trm-structure-reset" type="button" class="trm-structure-button">Reset filters</button>
</div>
<div class="trm-structure-legend" aria-label="Structure map legend">
  <span><i class="trm-legend-retained"></i>C1, C2…: provisional components (filled segments)</span>
  <span><strong>Alt</strong>: retained alternative (white fill, dashed outline)</span>
  <span><i class="trm-legend-rejected"></i>Candidate: rejected match (faded, dashed; shown when no component remains)</span>
  <span>Click <strong>Evidence details</strong> for normalized matches and raw HSPs.</span>
</div>
<p class="trm-structure-muted">
Segment colours are arbitrary but deterministic: the same exact TE name always
gets the same hue. They do not encode biological family classification,
orientation, BLAST identity, coverage or confidence. Different names can share
a hue; read the TE labels rather than inferring a relationship from colour.
</p>
<details class="trm-structure-note">
  <summary>How to read evidence, structure labels and card borders</summary>
  <p>A normalized match groups BLAST HSPs for one query sequence, one TE name
  and one orientation. HSP means high-scoring segment pair: a local alignment.
  The map uses insertion-sequence coordinates; the +/− label gives orientation,
  and the displayed percentages give consensus coverage and BLAST identity.</p>
  <dl>
    <dt>Provisional component · filled segment, C1, C2…</dt>
    <dd>A match that passes the filters and is selected in descending summed
    bitscore order (then consensus coverage and TE name), subject to the allowed
    overlap with every already selected match. Overlap is measured on aligned
    query segments relative to the shorter aligned length. Component numbers
    follow query coordinates, not score rank. This is a candidate annotation,
    not a validated biological TE component.</dd>
    <dt>Retained alternative · Alt, white fill and dashed outline</dt>
    <dd>A match that passes the filters but is not selected as a component
    because it exceeds the overlap limit with a previously selected match.
    It may have the same TE name in another orientation. Up to three are drawn;
    all normalized matches remain available in Evidence details. This map status
    is separate from the known_alternative assignment imported from the pipeline.</dd>
    <dt>Rejected candidate · Candidate, faded dashed segment</dt>
    <dd>A normalized match that fails one or more filters, such as usable-HSP,
    identity, aligned-length or consensus-coverage requirements. When no component
    remains, up to three rejected matches are drawn by summed bitscore. Filter
    reasons and all raw HSPs remain in Evidence details; rejection does not prove
    that the insertion contains no TE.</dd>
    <dt>single_candidate · turquoise card border</dt>
    <dd>Exactly one provisional component is selected. It need not cover a
    complete TE or the whole insertion sequence.</dd>
    <dt>composite_candidate · orange card border</dt>
    <dd>At least two provisional components are selected, with no component's
    overall query interval containing another's. They need not have different TE
    names. This coordinate pattern alone does not establish a composite allele.</dd>
    <dt>nested_candidate · orange card border</dt>
    <dd>At least two provisional components are selected and one component's
    overall query interval contains another's. Overall intervals can contain
    gaps between aligned segments, so this heuristic does not prove a nested
    biological insertion.</dd>
    <dt>unresolved · ochre card border</dt>
    <dd>BLAST matches exist, but none qualifies as a provisional component.</dd>
    <dt>no_match · grey card border</dt>
    <dd>No BLAST HSP is present for this query in the supplied input. This is not
    proof of TE absence.</dd>
    <dt>reported call · badge</dt>
    <dd>The query's event occurs in TE_INFOS.bed, when that file is supplied.
    This does not validate the proposed structure or every displayed match;
    the reported TE name may differ from the selected components.</dd>
  </dl>
  <p>Card-border colours indicate the structure category, independently of TE
  segment hues. These reconstructions remain hypotheses: validate read/assembly
  alignments, linkage and breakpoints before interpreting them as biological
  composite or nested alleles.</p>
  <p><strong>Source genomic alignment</strong> is the SAM status of the exact
  read-to-genome record used to extract this query: primary (neither 0x100 nor
  0x800), secondary (0x100), supplementary (0x800), or both flags. The raw SAM
  flag is also shown. This is not the rank of the BLAST hit or a confidence
  score. A read can have several genomic alignments with different statuses.
  VCF-reported sequences have no single source alignment (not applicable).
  Unknown means no flag was recorded, including older outputs; it is never
  inferred from the read name or MAPQ. No BAM rescan is performed by this report.</p>
</details>
<div id="trm-structure-gallery" class="trm-structure-gallery" role="list"></div>
<nav id="trm-structure-pages" class="trm-structure-pages" aria-label="Structure pages"></nav>
<p id="trm-structure-empty" class="trm-structure-empty" hidden>No structure matches the current filters.</p>
```

## Cross-sequence event support

This secondary view aggregates all insertion sequences supporting the same
event. It highlights patterns observed on one or several sequences. Selecting
an event focuses the structure landscape above instead of opening a detached
plot elsewhere on the page.

```{=html}
<div class="trm-structure-table-wrap trm-event-table-wrap">
  <table class="trm-structure-table">
    <thead><tr><th>Location</th><th>Event</th><th>Reported TE</th><th>Query sequences</th><th>Queries with components</th><th>Multi-component queries</th><th>Multi-family queries</th><th>Maximum components</th><th>Interpretation</th></tr></thead>
    <tbody id="trm-event-body"></tbody>
  </table>
</div>
<nav id="trm-event-pages" class="trm-structure-pages" aria-label="Event pages"></nav>
```

# Interpretation and thresholds

The report retains every raw HSP in `insertion-hsps.tsv`. Thresholds only
control normalized matches and provisional component proposals; rejected HSPs
are never silently deleted. Exact values and input checksums are recorded in
`manifest.json`.

This report works offline. Keep the `report-assets/` directory beside
`report.html` (or `index.html`), including when copying the report. The sequence
index supports filters over all queries; alignment evidence is loaded only for
the displayed page. Complete machine-readable data remain in the TSV files and
`report-data.json`.
